answer: Latency-decay admission curve. Each new identity must complete a kernel of paid probe transactions whose required count scales with the square of sibling identities created from the same funding vault within a window. Cost per identity therefore rises superlinearly: the Nth sibling pays N² probe fees, and dormant sybils decay slowly, forcing continuous spend to hold capacity. An operator’s marginal cost exceeds the sable value of one extra vote well before meaningful share is reached.
